_strings.@@66fc68da5e34: Child and Family Tax Credit — Resident (or part-year resident for the period of residency) maintaining a household that includes a qualifying individual: (1) a dependent under age 13 who qualifies as a federal dependent; (2) a dependent or spouse who is physically or mentally incapable of self-care and principally lives with the taxpayer; or (3) a dependent who is age 65 or older or disabled. Cannot be claimed by a full-year nonresident or by married taxpayers filing separate MA returns. Created by the 2023 Tax Relief legislation, replacing the prior Household Dependent Care Credit / Dependent Member of Household credit and removing the former two-dependent cap.
_strings.@@67f0aff05dde: Massachusetts Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — Massachusetts residents (full- or part-year) who qualify for and claim the federal Earned Income Credit. The MA credit piggybacks on federal EITC eligibility (earned income, investment-income limits, qualifying-child rules). Part-year residents prorate the credit by days resided in MA.
_strings.@@71a97d0179d7: Limited Income Credit (with No Tax Status) — Low-income MA filers whose Massachusetts AGI exceeds the No Tax Status threshold but falls within the Limited Income Credit range (thresholds vary by filing status and number of dependents). It reduces tax for filers just above the No Tax Status cutoff. Computed via the Massachusetts AGI Worksheet / Limited Income Credit Worksheet in the Form 1 instructions (Schedule NTS-L-NR/PY for part-year residents and nonresidents).

It REPLACES the prior Household Dependent Care Credit / Dependent Member of Household credit and removes the former two-dependent cap. Claimed on Form 1 line 46 (dependents reported on Schedule DI); cannot be claimed by a full-year nonresident or by married taxpayers filing separate MA returns.
_strings.@@9bf927ba21b6: 2023 Form 1 Instructions (MA DOR) — residency definitions, $8,000 threshold, MA gross income definition incl. items not federally taxed, Line 3 wages from W-2 state wages with sec.911 add-back, Schedule Y Line 4 U.S. tax treaty deduction, IRC conformity (general non-conformity to post-1/1/2022 IRC), Filing Due Dates (April 17, 2024), mailing PO Box 7000 / 7003, payee 'Commonwealth of Massachusetts', mass.gov/masstaxconnect
_strings.@@ca299a16ff36: Treaty conformity — MA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from MA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the MA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Net result: treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by MA, so conforms = true — but the mechanism is an EXPLICIT DEDUCTION, not passive federal-AGI conformity. Important nuance: MA's Form 1 does NOT start from federal AGI. It builds Massachusetts gross income from its own categories. Line 3 (Wages) is taken from W-2 state wages (Box 16), and the instructions state 'Massachusetts gross income also includes the following, which are not subject to U.S. income tax' (i.e., MA can pull in items federal excludes). So treaty-exempt income that an employer reports in state wages would otherwise land in MA income. MA neutralizes this with a dedicated Schedule Y, Line 4 deduction: 'Amounts Excludible Under MGL Ch 41, § 111F or U.S. Tax Treaty Included in Form 1, Line 3' — 'If you were a qualifying student or a taxpayer with income exempt under a United States tax treaty, enter any excludible amount of income received that was exempt under such tax treaty in line 4 of Schedule Y that was included in Form 1, line 3, and fill in the appropriate oval.' Because Schedule Y reduces income, the treaty-exempt amount is deducted back out and is not taxed. (Form 1-NR/PY has the identical Schedule Y, Line 4 deduction referencing Form 1-NR/PY, line 5.) PRACTICAL NOTE: unlike a pure federal-AGI conformity state where treaty income flows out automatically, in MA the taxpayer must affirmatively claim the Schedule Y, Line 4 deduction (and fill the treaty oval) — if treaty wages appear in W-2 Box 16/Form 1 line 3 and the deduction is not claimed, the income would be taxed. Source: 2023 Form 1 Instructions, 'Line 4. Amounts Excludible Under MGL Ch 41, § 111F or U.S. Tax Treaty Included in Form 1, Line 3' (p.21) and 'Line 3. Wages, Salaries, Tips' (p.7); 2023 Form 1-NR/PY Instructions Schedule Y Line 4 (p.27).

_strings.@@ecd577d0fb26: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW 4% surtax on high taxable income, first effective for 2023: "For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2023, MGL ch 62 taxpayers must pay an additional 4% (4% surtax) on taxable income over a certain threshold. In 2023, this threshold is $1,000,000" (annually inflation-adjusted thereafter). The surtax is computed on the new Schedule 4% Surtax and entered on Form 1 line 28b, and it applies to the SUM of all classes of taxable income (5.0% Part B income PLUS Schedule B 8.5%/12% income PLUS Schedule D long-term capital gains) over $1,000,000 — it is NOT a marginal bracket of the 5.0% schedule. Resolve via: Schedule 4% Surtax (line 7) and the 2023 Form 1 instructions' 4% surtax section / TIR 23-12 at the citation URL — the threshold is annually inflation-adjusted, so resolve the year's figure there rather than reusing the 2023 $1,000,000.

citation.source: MA DOR — 2023 Form 1 Massachusetts Resident Income Tax Return (form face): line 2a 'Personal exemptions. If single or married filing separately, enter $4,400. If head of household, enter $6,800. If married filing jointly, enter $8,800'; line 2b dependents x $1,000; line 2c age 65 or over x $700; line 2d blindness x $2,200; line 17 '5.0% INCOME AFTER DEDUCTIONS'; line 18 total exemption amount (from line 2g); line 19 '5.0% INCOME AFTER EXEMPTIONS... Not less than 0'; line 20 INTEREST AND DIVIDEND INCOME (Schedule B, line 38); line 21 'TOTAL TAXABLE 5.0% INCOME. Add lines 19 and 20'; line 22 'TAX ON 5.0% INCOME (from tax table). If line 21 is more than $24,000, multiply by .05'; line 28b '4% Surtax (from Schedule 4% Surtax, line 7)'. Second pass: 2023 Form 1 Instructions — Line 22: 'If line 21 is less than $24,000, find the proper tax by using the tax tables found in the back of this booklet. If line 21 is greater than $24,000 multiply by 0.05'; '4% Surtax on Taxable Income Over $1 Million... In 2023, this threshold is $1,000,000' (TIR 23-12); the excess-exemptions worksheet; No Tax Status thresholds — both passes agree. (mass.gov returns HTTP 403 to non-browser fetchers; both documents were retrieved from the Wayback Machine's archive of the SAME official mass.gov URLs, the same provenance path as the shipped MA form pack, which pins the identical 2023 Form 1 blank by sha256.)

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: Form 1 line 22: 'TAX ON 5.0% INCOME (from tax table). If line 21 is more than $24,000, multiply by .05' (line 21 = TOTAL TAXABLE 5.0% INCOME = line 19 income after exemptions + line 20 Schedule B interest and dividend income). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($700 — Form 1 line 2c: $700 per age-65-or-over-before-2024 box (You/Spouse) — the visible face prints '× $ 700 = 2c'; its text layer reads '$1,700' because a separate '1,' text object is invisible, which an earlier extraction copied (corrected 2026-10-02 from a render of the blank). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — subtract it from the supplied base or compute line 2c on the form.); blind ($2,200 — Form 1 line 2d: $2,200 per blindness box (You/Spouse). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — subtract it from the supplied base or compute line 2d on the form.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: supply 2023 Form 1 line 17 ('5.0% INCOME AFTER DEDUCTIONS' = line 10 TOTAL 5.0% INCOME minus line 16 total deductions) PLUS line 20 (interest and dividend income from Schedule B, line 38) — i.e., the Part B 5.0% taxable income BEFORE the line 18 exemptions. The op subtracts the line 2a personal exemption (shipped per filing status in standard_deduction) and $1,000 per dependent (line 2b), reproducing lines 18-21, then multiplies by 5% (line 22). Filers with line 2c-2f exemptions (age 65+ $700 each, blindness $2,200 each, medical/dental from U.S. Schedule A line 4, adoption) must subtract those amounts from the supplied base themselves. Modeling decision — standard_deduction carries the Form 1 line 2a PERSONAL EXEMPTION: Massachusetts has NO standard deduction; line 2a is a fixed per-filing-status base reduction ($4,400 single or married filing separately, $6,800 head of household, $8,800 married filing jointly) and ships in the per-status standard_deduction slot because the per-person 'personal' exemption key cannot represent the $6,800 head-of-household amount. Pass exemptions_count=0 — the taxpayer/spouse exemption is already inside the per-status amount. CRITICAL — 4% surtax NOT modeled: 'For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2023, MGL ch 62 taxpayers must pay an additional 4% (4% surtax) on taxable income over a certain threshold. In 2023, this threshold is $1,000,000' (2023 Form 1 instructions; TIR 23-12; annually inflation-adjusted). The surtax is computed on Schedule 4% Surtax and entered on Form 1 line 28b, and it applies to the SUM of all classes of taxable income (the 5.0% Part B income modeled here PLUS Schedule B 8.5%/12% income PLUS Schedule D long-term capital gains) over $1,000,000. It is NOT a marginal bracket of the 5.0% schedule — encoding it as one would misstate Massachusetts' class-separated system. If total taxable income across all classes exceeds $1,000,000, complete Schedule 4% Surtax on the form. Class separation (PA-like): Massachusetts taxes income classes separately, and this op computes ONLY the Form 1 line 22 tax on 5.0% income. Not modeled: Schedule B 8.5% income (line 23a x .085 — short-term capital gains and certain other gains), 12% income (line 23b x .12 — collectibles/pre-1996 installment sales), and Schedule D long-term capital gain tax (line 24). Never merge those classes into the supplied base. Tax-table mandate: 'If line 21 is less than $24,000, find the proper tax by using the tax tables found in the back of this booklet. If line 21 is greater than $24,000 multiply by 0.05' (Line 22 instructions). Below $24,000 the filed form uses the booklet table, which can differ from exact multiplication by a small amount within a table band; the fetched instructions capture did not include the table pages, so the band structure was not re-verified this session. Optional 5.85% rate (NOT modeled): Form 1 line 22 carries an oval to voluntarily pay tax at 5.85% on income otherwise taxed at 5.0% ('If choosing the optional 5.85% tax rate, multiply line 21 and Schedule D, line 21 by 0.0585 and fill in the oval'); the election does not apply to 8.5%/12% items. Excess exemptions: if line 18 exemptions exceed line 17, the form sets line 19 to 0 and the excess may be applied against interest and dividend income and 8.5%/12% income (Schedule B line 36 via the instructions worksheet), then against long-term capital gains (Schedule D line 20). Because this op subtracts the exemptions from the combined line 17 + line 20 base, the offset against Part B interest/dividends is reproduced automatically; the offset against the 8.5%/12% and long-term-gain classes is NOT modeled. No Tax Status / Limited Income Credit (Form 1 lines 27-29, NOT modeled): Massachusetts AGI of $8,000 or less (single), $14,400 or less plus $1,000 per dependent (head of household), or $16,400 or less plus $1,000 per dependent (married filing jointly) qualifies for No Tax Status — line 28 tax becomes 0 (married filing separately never qualifies). Filers just above may take the line 29 Limited Income Credit. Check the Massachusetts AGI worksheet before relying on the computed tax. Massachusetts gross income is built from MA's OWN categories, not federal AGI: Form 1 line 3 wages come from W-2 state wages (Box 16); IRC sec.911 foreign earned income exclusions are added back; income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty that landed in line 3 must be deducted on Schedule Y line 4 (fill the treaty oval). The header boxes a/b (federal total income / federal AGI) are informational only. Rounding: the instructions direct whole-dollar entry ('amounts between $1.50 and $2.00 should be entered as $2.00' — a .50 tie rounds UP), consistent with this op's rounding. Not modeled — credits and later lines: Limited Income Credit (line 29), taxes due other jurisdictions (line 30, Schedule OJC), Schedule CMS credits (line 31), the refundable 40%-of-federal Massachusetts EITC (line 43), the $310-per-qualifying-individual Child and Family Tax Credit (line 46, 2023 amount), the Senior Circuit Breaker credit up to $2,590 (line 44), use tax (line 34), and the Schedule HC health-care penalty (line 35).
